name: Burning Rate Emulator (ACME BRE)
fuel: Gaseous ethylene/N2 on a 25 mm porous burner, emulating solid and liquid fuels
key_findings: All flames at 21% O2 self-extinguished within 40 s; steady flames were seen at 26.5%, 34% and 40% O2.
59 successfully ignited tests; NASA human-habitat atmospheres were used.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II (BASS-II)
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE flow duct
fuel: Thin and thick flat samples, PMMA slabs, spheres and cylinders, cotton/fiberglass fabric
key_findings: Flames are very sensitive to airflow between 0 and 5 cm/s; they survive below 1 cm/s as dim blue flames and can flare up quickly when airflow increases.
Most tests had heat release rates well below 100 W.
First ISS use of MSG volume dilution with nitrogen to lower oxygen.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
fuel: Solid samples of different shapes, including cotton/fiberglass fabric
key_findings: One of the first investigations of extinguishing fuels burning in microgravity; assessed nitrogen as a suppressant.

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire I–III)
hardware: Uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle after leaving the ISS
fuel: Cotton/fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric, 40.6 x 94 cm; Saffire II: smaller material samples
key_findings: First large-scale fire inside a spacecraft; the sample was an order of magnitude larger than earlier microgravity tests.
Concurrent flames reached a steady size and spread rate instead of accelerating as they do on Earth.
Saffire II objective: verify oxygen flammability limits in low gravity.

name: Saffire IV–V
fuel: PMMA, cotton fabric, cotton/fiberglass blend, Nomex; samples 40 cm wide
key_findings: Tested exploration-like atmospheres (~26% O2 at ~71 kPa).
Extinguishment of thin charring fuels at increased oxygen cannot be assumed to happen rapidly.
An upstream flame's oxygen 'shadow' inhibited or extinguished downstream flames.
Heat release up to 10 kW, yet average vehicle conditions stayed acceptable.
note: Verify whether this dataset is in PSI.

name: Saffire VI
hardware: Uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle, far-field diagnostics
key_findings: Smoke and gaseous products, not heat, are the main hazard to crew.
Studied fire impact on the vehicle and post-fire recovery.
note: Verify whether this dataset is in PSI.

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
fuel: Overheated Teflon, Kapton, cellulose, silicone rubber, dibutylphthalate
key_findings: A substantial portion of smoke particles were below 500 nm.
The ISS light-scattering detector often missed the small particles from Teflon and Kapton, both widely used in electronics.

name: SAME Reflight (SAME-R)
key_findings: Expedition 24 (2010): added diagnostics and an expanded test matrix to guide future smoke detector design.

name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT, DAFT-2)
hardware: One of the SAME smoke instruments, used to measure dust
key_findings: Background dust matters for detector design: it can trigger false alarms (relevant for dusty lunar habitats).

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
key_findings: Limiting oxygen index in O2/N2: ~0.15 for heptane, ~0.12 for methanol.
Tested CO2 and helium dilution as suppressants.
Discovered 'cool flames': heptane droplets kept burning invisibly after the visible flame went out — hot-flame-only safety procedures may be inadequate.

name: FLEX-2
key_findings: Follow-on droplet combustion study of burning and extinction physics.

name: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI)
key_findings: Follow-on to FLEX studying the cool-flame regime of droplet burning.

name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (ACME CFI-G)
hardware: CIR, ACME insert, spherical porous burner
fuel: Ethane, propane, n-butane; normal and inverse (inside-out) flames
key_findings: Highest-oxygen microgravity tests in PSI: up to 85% O2 flowing from the burner (inverse flames).
First spherical cool diffusion flames of gaseous fuels — only obtained for n-butane at 2 bar and 39% O2.

name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME E-FIELD)
key_findings: Electric fields acting on flame ions mimic partial gravity — the closest thing in PSI to Moon/Mars gravity data.
Showed potential to reduce emissions from non-premixed flames.

name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME s-Flame)
key_findings: Flame growth and extinction data for improving computational models.

name: Flame Design (ACME)
key_findings: First quasi-steady non-premixed spherical flames; larger flames died from radiative heat loss.
Studied soot production to design soot-free, robust flames.

name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME CLD Flame)
fuel: Gaseous fuels from pure (sooty) to highly diluted
key_findings: Benchmark data at sooty and near-extinction extremes for computational models.

name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE)
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), fan-driven flow duct
key_findings: Smoke point of gas jet flames in co-flow; its flow duct was reused by BASS, BASS-II and SLICE.

name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE flow duct
key_findings: Flame structure and liftoff (2012); precursor to ACME's CLD Flame.

name: Cool Flame Dynamics CFD Analysis (ground study using FLEX data)
key_findings: Uses FLEX flight data from PSI to quantify how external thermal and convective perturbations affect cool flames.
